chunks: ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Sabāṭī wrote to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام.
He asked him about a man to whom another man had left a bequest that three men perform hajj on his behalf: is it permissible for him to take one hajj share for himself from them?
So he عليه السلام wrote in reply in his own handwriting, and I read it:
"Perform hajj on his behalf, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills. For you shall have the like of his reward, and nothing will be diminished from his reward, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills."

key_terms.أَوْصَى: left a bequest or final instruction
key_terms.حَجَّةً: one act of hajj or one hajj assignment
key_terms.يُحِجَّ: to perform hajj on behalf of someone

ai.seo_question: Can a trustee who is instructed to arrange hajj for others perform one of the hajj acts himself on behalf of the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a bequest for hajj on behalf of a deceased person. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام permits the entrusted person to perform one of those hajj acts himself on the deceased’s behalf, while affirming that the performer receives equal reward without diminishing the reward of the deceased.
